newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Ciampi sees November inflation 2.7-2.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Ciampi sees November inflation 2.7-2.8 pct.

text.p: Italian inflation should fall to 2.7 or 2.8 percent year-on-year in November, meaning an average inflation rate of 2.5 percent in 1997 is now feasible, Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said in an interview on Friday.
"Inflation is now certainly below three percent," Ciampi told financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore.

"If it is true that we will end October with 3.1 percent -- some hope for 3.0 percent -- in November, we will fall to 2.7-2.8 percent. And then, the hypothesis of 2.5-percent inflation is no longer a hope, it is a probability," he said.

Preliminary inflation data from sample 10 cities this week pointed to a year-on-year October rate of 3.0 percent and prompted the Bank of Italy to cut its key discount rate by 75 basis points to 7.5 percent on Wedenesday, a month earlier than expected.
Inflation was 3.4 percent year-on-year in September. Final official consumer price data for October are due on November 7.
"With November at 2.7-2.8 percent, prices would have to go up 2.2 percent to 2.3 percent in December next year to reach an average 2.5 percent in 1997," Ciampi said.
